About this sketch & build plan +

September 7, 2026. Fresh pencil-drawn field-chart prototype. Warm fibrous paper, subtle folds, chart grid, handwritten headings, and a small boat moving among day markers. The painted ocean now surrounds the whole sheet. Earlier references: KIKK’s bold type and clear structure, Hack the North’s substantial illustration, and the heavily painted ocean pattern in The Marvelous Misadventures of Flapjack. This supersedes the split paper/ocean layout.

Design

  • Schedule opens immediately, with the official HackIllinois logo.
  • A fibrous, folded paper chart sits within the ocean scene. Soft shadows and irregular edges separate paper from water; event text remains on quiet paper.
  • Eight independently moving wave rows use three different painted wave bands. Each row drifts and rises on its own rhythm; day selection sends a staggered swell through them. Day selection moves a small drawn boat along a route and moves each wave row horizontally over 2.6 seconds, with different distances and a staggered rise-and-fall motion. Nearer waves move farther. Paper stays fixed; Pause ocean and reduced-motion settings make day changes immediate.
  • Sample day selection, category filters, saved-only view, bookmarks, and details use native HTML controls and CSS. Favorites do not persist after reload.
  • No live API connection in this design preview.

React build

  1. Resolve Git setup before application implementation; Git has not been initialized.
  2. Write failing tests for API event parsing, time grouping, filtering, and persistent saved events.
  3. Build React schedule with public API reads, search, real event dates, and loading/error/empty states.
  4. Implement the chosen illustration and motion while keeping content accessible.
  5. Check desktop, phone, keyboard, reduced motion, live API behavior, and production build.
  6. Finish the required HTML handoff with changed files and evidence.

Sources and limits

The official logo is embedded unchanged from the 2021 website asset. Original ocean artwork generated for this project, stored in planning/artwork/wave-layers.png and embedded here so this file works alone. Reference: KIKK and Hack the North.

The API documentation describes public GET /event/ reads. Live API behavior is still unverified. This disposable HTML prototype has no React dependencies, authentication, or deployment. Browser behavior checks, rather than application unit tests, apply at this design stage.
